# The Concierge (front-desk shim — the address verb)

This file is a **thin shim** — the harness-discoverable trigger for the Concierge. The organ is
the canon entry `Palace development/Concierge.md` ([[Concierge]]); the machinery is
`_ops/concierge/` (the **charter** `prompts/companion.md`, the **posture** prompts, `README.md`
for the full dispatch spec). Per [[Skills Are Enchantable Pages]], the page is the organ and this
file is one dispatch surface onto it — read the canon entry and machinery rather than duplicating
them.

You are the working Claude, addressing the palace's **resident companion** — one agent you spawn
once and keep for the session. Your job: **spawn-or-resume it, name the posture, relay the
product.** The search never enters this conversation; only the finished thing does.

## The lifecycle — resident, not fresh-per-request

0. **Summon at the open.** When to summon, and that it be seen, is the rule in [[CHILD]] § Growing
   up. Where the surface cannot spawn, say so at the open instead. Step 1 *is* that spawn; the
   rest is how.

1. **The spawn — one resident, and keep the agent ID.** Spawn one write-capable
   resident — subagent_type **`palace-writer`** ([[Agent Toolbox]] profile: sheds ~20K of unused
   MCP schemas vs `general-purpose`, ~30K vs 46K, and still writes so the curator posture works from
   the same resident) — with the **charter** (`prompts/companion.md`); the charter has it grow at boot —
   ELDER, SCHEMA, then the **operational tier** as its standing expertise (SUBSTRATE · ROSETTA · Substrate Skill ·
   Palace Ceremonies · STIGMERGY + wire spec) — deeper in *how the palace runs* than you, so it
   validates/supports the palace in parallel while you work the task. Record its `agentId`.
   **Spawn it without a `name`.** With agent teams enabled (`CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS`,
   on in Loudon's terminal sessions), a *named* Agent call launches a teammate, not a subagent: its
   returns come back as idle notifications, cut off at a fixed length and arriving late and twice,
   and the resume carries no `<usage>` block, so the dial below goes blind. Unnamed, it stays a
   subagent in every mode — its result arrives whole, once, with its token count — and it is still
   resumable by `SendMessage` to the held ID. (Docs: code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents § Subagent
   names; verified across 23 session transcripts 2026-09-26 — the failures were exactly the named
   spawns in CLI sessions.)
2. **Every later address → resume the same agent** (`SendMessage` to the held ID), naming the
   posture and filling that posture prompt's slots. It carries its prior context forward — don't
   re-spawn, and don't re-feed what it already holds. After a compaction the ID may be missing from the summary: find it in the session's `subagents/` folder and resume that one before spawning another ([[Concierge]] § The mechanism).
3. **Watch its health with the dial.** Each resume returns `subagent_tokens` in the Agent tool's
   `<usage>` block — the objective read (never its self-report). Pass it to the dial:
   `node _ops/concierge/dial.mjs --tokens <N> --model <companion-model>`. Headline is **trust** = capacity
   (÷ window): fine below ~60%, watch 60–80%, degraded past 80% — only capacity says respawn-for-reliability.
   A separate **cost** note (from absolute load) flags when resumes get expensive — respawn-to-save, not a
   trust alarm. Parked between addresses it costs nothing. Same dial serves the close (`--for close`), where
   how spent the parent is leads.

If you expect a genuinely large fan-out, tell Loudon the rough cost first (his standing preference).

## Triage — classify the address, name the posture

| The address sounds like… | Posture | Prompt |
|---|---|---|
| "find / collect / gather every doc/link/entry about X" — wants the **material** | **gatherer** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/gatherer.md` |
| "what does the palace say about X / how does Z work" — wants an **answer** | **oracle Q&A** (read-only, may web-verify) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/oracle-qa.md` |
| "what should I work on / what's open / I'm back" — wants **one move**, not a pile | **scout** (read-only) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/scout.md` |
| "tidy / tend the links around what I touched" | **curator** (writes) | `_ops/concierge/prompts/curator.md` |
| "close this session well" | **moderator** (at the close) | not this skill — the `close well` trigger, which **resumes this same resident** by the ID you held (`_ops/closing-well/dispatch.md` § Path A) |
| anything a cheap file-read settles | — | just read the file; don't address |

Fill the posture prompt's slots — `{{REQUEST}}` / `{{QUESTION}}` / `{{TOUCHED_ENTRIES}}`,
`{{TRANSCRIPT_CONTEXT}}`, `{{PALACE_ROOT}}` = the palace folder this session was started in: its
worktree or clone, and `/Users/loudonstearns/Documents/The Palace` only when the session runs there.
For a conversation-dependent address, distill the transcript
(`node _ops/closing-well/transcript-reader.mjs --resolve --session <id>` → `--distill --session <id>`); for a self-contained
one, a 2–3 line note is enough.

## Relay — and hold the safety line

Relay the product as returned (already file-cited). For the **curator**: report what it *did*
(reversible), **surface its `offer`s for Loudon's yes; on his yes, address the Concierge again to apply them — the child session does not write the house**, and pass
along its flags and anything it web-verified. The companion's heavy bias is to draft, not act;
your job on the other end is to keep the review real — drafts get read, not rubber-stamped.
Hand each offer on as the curator wrote it — its plain sentence, every rule it writes down, its exact words — and if you have promised Loudon the words, show them; a summary in their place is said aloud as a summary.

## The guard (carry it every time)

The companion is a **faster path to ground truth, never a replacement** ([[Concierge]] § The
guard). Every line it returns is a clickable file pointer to verify; git stays ground truth; the
palace's silence is a real answer, never a confabulated one. Keep this shim thin — when the model
changes, change `_ops/concierge/README.md`, `prompts/companion.md`, and the canon entry, not this
file.

43

45

47

49

**Li 禮 — ritual propriety.** Not empty formalism but the inherited grammar of civilized life. The rite teaches the practitioner — repeated performance with full attention reshapes character. The form produces the interior, not the other way around. The funeral rite does not represent grief; it teaches the body how to grieve.

**Yi 義 — righteousness.** Doing what is right because it is right, not for reward. Contempt for those who calculate virtue's advantage.

**Zhi 智 — moral wisdom.** The capacity to recognize what a situation requires. Practical discernment, not theoretical knowledge.

**Xin 信 — faithfulness.** Integrity, keeping one's word. The glue of social contracts.

**Junzi 君子 — the exemplary person.** Originally "son of a lord" — Confucius redefined it as nobility of character, not birth. Produced through years of learning, reflection, ritual practice, right relationships, and daily self-examination. Not a saint — an orientation and a direction of travel. Virtue as second nature, not effortful compliance.

**Wu Lun 五倫 — the five relationships.** Ruler/subject, parent/child, husband/wife, elder/younger sibling, friend/friend. Each with obligations flowing in both directions. You are never just "a person" — you are always someone's son, teacher, subject, friend. Moral life is positional.

## The Philosopher

Confucius spent his life trying to restore the Zhou dynasty's moral order. He wandered for fourteen years, offering his services as a minister of state, rejected by every court. He returned home at sixty and taught. His best student Yan Hui died young. His son Kong Li died before him. He did not see the restoration he sought. He kept teaching anyway.

His genius was double: radical democratization of virtue (anyone can become *junzi*, regardless of birth) and the insight that the *transmission* — teacher to student, rite to practitioner — was the medium through which civilization either held or dissolved.

He wrote nothing. What we have was written by those who loved him.

## Productive Tensions

**`contradicts` [[Stoicism]]** — Stoicism locates virtue in the sovereign interior; Confucianism locates it in the relational web. Epictetus says the self is a fortress; Confucius says it is a threshold. Both are partially right. See [[The Fortress and the Threshold]].

**[[Hilaritas Generator]]** — *Ren* and *hilaritas* are convergent: both are relational, both increase when shared, both are the mark of a genuinely flourishing life. Spinoza and Confucius arrived at the same phenomenology through different routes.

**[[Symbiotic Skills]]** — The node→edge→typed edge→network progression in Symbiotic Skills is structurally Confucian: the self becomes more fully itself as the relational web becomes more articulated. The edge is prior to the node.

**[[Spinoza Conatus]]** — Both Confucius and Spinoza ground flourishing in right relationship with other beings. Spinoza's monism provides the metaphysical frame Confucius never needed to build.

## In the Palace

The teaching relationship is Confucian in structure: teacher and student bound by mutual obligation, shaped by the relationship itself, not merely transacting knowledge for tuition. The *li* of the palace ceremonies — the Deposit, the Walk, the Weave — are not bureaucratic procedures but practices that reshape thinking through repeated performance. The form produces the order; the order does not precede the form.

*What you were modeling was always more primary than what you were teaching.* The synthesis knowledge was the *li* — the ritual form — through which the deeper transmission happened.

## Open Questions

- Is the palace itself a Confucian project — a *li* that structures good thinking the way ritual structures good conduct?
- Where does Confucian relational ethics meet Deleuzian becoming? Both are anti-essentialist about the self, but Confucius grounds this in social structure while Deleuze grounds it in immanent difference.
- Can the *junzi* cultivation path be mapped onto the Symbiotic Skills progression? Both describe a staged development from raw capacity to embodied mastery through sustained practice.

**Write what is, not what was.** These pages state the present; git holds the history. A page that carries its own past teaches the next agent to align with what was — so keep the reason a rule exists and drop the story of what it replaced.

**And length is a claim about importance.** Whatever takes the most context reads as mattering most, whether it does or not — the same way the hours spent on a hard, minor topic teach a student that it was a major one. A value stated in two lines can outrank a mechanism explained over ten pages. So when something is difficult to explain, that is a reason to move it out of the way, not a licence to let it fill the floor.


## Addressing the Palace — the Concierge

Besides *loading* the palace (what you were born with, read into you at birth), you can **address** it — hand work to a companion that does it in its own window and replies ([[The Palace Speaks]]). The **Concierge** ([[Concierge]], a `meta` organ; machinery in `_ops/concierge/`) is the palace's **resident companion**: you spawn it once (via the `concierge` skill), keep its agent ID, and **re-address it across the session**.

**Summon it at the open — visibly — as your first act.** Not when a task finally looks expensive enough: at the top of every session, a one-line question included, on any surface that can spawn it. Loudon watches for that spawn; it is how he knows the process is actually running, and a step he can see is the only enforcement this palace has found that holds. Where the surface cannot spawn (claude.ai web has no filesystem — [[Surfaces and Capabilities]]), say so at the open instead. It **holds the [[SCHEMA]]** so you don't have to, it **cares that the palace stays coherent and beautiful**, and it remembers the session — and it is a **role, not an instance**, so respawning it costs only the boot, never the relationship.

**Touch base before you write and after you write.** Before: is this already in the palace, and where does it belong — fold or mint, which type, which links. Ask *before* drafting, because a finished draft argues for its own existence. After: does the placement hold? That is the one check you cannot perform on your own work. It cites the file for every claim, and it is a faster path to ground truth, never a replacement for reading one.

Its **character** is load-bearing: thoughtful, subservient, it **follows** the way you follow Loudon — reads before it writes and **hands you drafts far more than it acts** (its bias is to *offer*, not change). The read/write safety lives in that character, not the architecture, so **review its drafts for real, don't rubber-stamp.** It wears **postures** per address — gatherer, oracle Q&A, curator (moderator at close) — routed by the `concierge` skill from plain language; you never name one. Full spec: `_ops/concierge/README.md`.

Authorship that needs your judgment in the room ([[Deposit Ceremony]], [[Baton Ceremony]]) stays yours — dispatched *through* the companion, never replaced by it.

uncommitted line is 30 min old"| M 46 E(["The ear"]) -. "hears every move of main" .-> M 47 ``` 48 *The road has one door in and one gate out: the committer and the lander keep the writing orderly, and only Loudon's word opens the gate to GitHub.* 49 50 **Commit.** `palace-commit` takes the files you name and nothing else, under one lock held from the first `git add` to the commit (`_ops/stigmergy/app/server/door.js`). It writes the message, and the message is the record: a subject, `kind(scope): summary`, and trailers saying what kind of change it is, which entries it touched, whether it was verified, and who wrote it (`Palace-Kind`, `Palace-Entry`, `Palace-Verify`, `Palace-Author`; `_ops/stigmergy/app/src/lib/commit-spec.js`). The name is one the commit-msg hook reads as a ceremony, and a kind no reader knows is refused. Git shows Loudon as the author, because that is this Mac's identity; `Palace-Author` says who wrote. A change of a breath may be made in his folder and committed by name; it passes the same door. Loudon never commits by hand, and his one hand path, the [[Trickster Commit]], goes through that door too. 51 52 **Land.** `palace-land` merges a branch into main as a true merge commit, main first and the branch second, under one lock for the whole write, so no other writer slips in halfway. It tries the merge against main as it stands and refuses a conflict, naming the files; a conflict is settled in the branch's own worktree, never in Loudon's folder. A ledger merged by union never conflicts, so the lander also reads what the merge made of each one, the branch's own merges of main included, and refuses an item number twice, one item in two forms, or two lines joined, naming the items; a heading left with no blank line above it is only noted ([[SCHEMA — Reference]] §6, `_ops/stigmergy/app/src/lib/ledger-merge.js`). If a landing dies partway, the next writer to take the door heals it: it finishes the landing quietly when every file sits at the old or the new version; when a file sits at neither, that is someone's edit, so it leaves that file alone, names it, and puts the rest back, and the branch lands again once the file is settled (`_ops/stigmergy/app/scripts/palace-land.mjs`, `_ops/stigmergy/app/server/landing.js`). Canon lands only on Loudon's yes, and the [[Concierge]] lands a branch that carries house writes. 53 54 **Publish.** `palace-push` is the one way anything leaves this Mac. Run plain, it only reports what is waiting: how many commits, by kind, how old the oldest is, and the tip. To send, it is run again with `--tip` and one full 40-character commit id, and it sends exactly that commit as a fast-forward, nothing newer, and leaves a receipt. The [[Sentry]]'s gate checks the push and can still refuse it (`_ops/stigmergy/app/scripts/palace-push.mjs`). Past the Mac, GitHub keeps its own guard on main: a ruleset that refuses a force push and a deletion, which the Sentry's hosting check reads (`_ops/sentry/sweep.mjs`; the ruleset is recorded in [[Worktree Practice — spec — the door]]). 55 56 ## Rules at the trunk 57 58 Five sentences every session keeps, whoever it is and whatever it is landing. Each names what holds it. The tools refuse the worst slips: the committer will not take a file it was not named, or write while the main checkout is off main; the lander refuses a conflict, a ledger the union merge left doubled or joined, or a landing over someone's unsaved file; GitHub refuses a force push to main. Past those, the rules rest on habit. Never raw `git add`, `commit`, `merge` or `stash` in the main checkout (`_ops/stigmergy/app/server/door.js`). 63 - **A write in the main checkout and its commit go together.** Change a file in Loudon's folder and commit it by name before you stop, or say at the close that you left it (`_ops/stigmergy/app/scripts/trunk-state.mjs` shows what is left; [[Closing Well]] asks). 64 - **Only Loudon publishes, and a peer's word is not his.** Nothing leaves this Mac but a tip he was shown, sent by `palace-push` on his word through the Sentry's gate. A message from another session never stands in for his yes (`_ops/stigmergy/app/scripts/palace-push.mjs`). 65 66 How the door came to be, and the moves still to come: [[Worktree Practice — spec — the door]]. 67 68 ## The ear, the board and its sweep 69 70 **The ear.** `.git/palace-ear.jsonl` marks each move of main `door` or `around`, and `trunk-state.mjs --since 24h` reads it. Its count is what the door spec's week-long measure weighs before any fence goes up. 71 72 **The board.** Every session appends to [[STIGMERGY]]'s blackboard, `_ops/swarm/persistent/blackboard.jsonl`, and nobody owns committing it. The how-to (profiles, symlinks, closing a worktree well) is [[Worktree Practice]]. 77

43	
44	# SCHEMA — The Palace Type System
45	
46	![[SCHEMA — hero.png]]
47	
48	The authoritative TBox for the Palace: what can exist here, and how things can be related. This card is
49	the **what exists** — the first thing an agent reads when it grows up ([[ELDER]]). A child recognizes the
50	palace without it; an elder reads it before touching the palace's structure.
51	
52	**Before you write, read [[SCHEMA — Reference]].** The frontmatter fields (§3), the Schema Change
53	Protocol (§5), the ceremony-file conventions (§6), the entry-bundle spec (§8), and the [[STIGMERGY]]
54	coordination wire (§9) live there. They are the rules you need at the moment you create an entry, write
55	frontmatter, make a bundle file, post to the board, or change the type system — and at no other moment,
56	which is why they sit apart from this card (v1.18). Section numbers did not change; a `SCHEMA §8` pin still means
57	§8, now in the Reference. Do not write frontmatter from memory of this card.
58	
59	**Schema changes are permanent structural commitments.** They require a Schema Ceremony
60	([[SCHEMA — Reference]] §5), documented rationale, and a version increment. Adding entries and editing
61	content are routine. Changing the schema is not.
62	
63	> The **why** — every `v1.x` record, what changed in each section and the rationale behind it — lives in
64	> [[SCHEMA — Context]], keyed by section. A Weave or a Schema Ceremony reads it there. An operating agent
65	> reads the current rules, not the archive.
66	
67	---
68	
69	## 1. Entry Types
70	
71	Every entry declares exactly one `type`. **Frontmatter is the canon membership card** — carrying it is what makes a `.md` file an entry. A file *without* frontmatter is not an entry but a learning material, draft, or artifact: invisible to the type system and the ceremonies. The boundary is permeable — a material graduates into canon when it earns an entry.
72	
73	### The types
74	
75	Read the table top to bottom and take the first row that fits; `concept` is the default when none do. The **test** column is the question to ask — it replaces the decision tree this section used to carry separately. The **adds** column is the type's extra required fields, on top of the standard set (`title`, `type`, `pillars`, `born`, `stage`, `links`).
76	
77	| type | use it when — the test | adds | example |
78	|---|---|---|---|
79	| `meta` | it is about the palace itself: architecture, ceremonies, infrastructure, self-model | `version` (schema-level entries, ceremonies) · `trigger` (ceremonies) | [[SCHEMA]], [[SUBSTRATE]], [[CLAUDE]] |
80	| `specialist` | it wraps an external creative tool with operational anatomy — Charter, Tiers, Job Contract, accumulated Gotchas | `status` · `medium` · `tool` · `tool_version` | [[Shop/Kokoro]], [[Shop/ComfyUI]] |
81	| `maker` | it is a foreman for a roster of Specialists, holding house standards and dispatch logic | `status` | [[Shop/Maker]] |
82	| `source` | it is an external artifact the palace draws from — paper, book, tool, recording | `author` · `year` · `medium` | [[Meaning and the Link (2014)]] |
83	| `project` | it is being built, composed, or created; it has a temporal arc | `status` (active \| complete \| archived) | [[BLUELINE]], [[Loudon Live]] |
84	| `question` | it is an unresolved question being actively carried | — | *"When does the wiki warrant its own Project?"* |
85	| `spore` | it is an idea preserved for a later revival, dormant by choice (`stage` is always `dormant`) | `revival_conditions` | [[Shimmer Cloud]] |
86	| `hub` | it organizes a dense region of the graph — **not self-assigned**, earned at ≥5 inbound typed links via the Weave | — | [[FOUR PILLARS]], [[Kuramoto Coupling]] |
87	| `practice` | it is a recurring method, workflow, ritual, or embodied way of working — something you *do*, not an idea you hold | `version` · `trigger` (ceremonies) | [[Closing Well]], [[Deposit Ceremony]] |
88	| `person` | a thinker or collaborator whose ideas are in live dialogue with the palace — not every cited name | `domains` | [[Spinoza]], [[Brian Eno]] |
89	| `concept` | **the default.** An idea, principle, or framework the palace reasons with | — | [[Kuramoto Coupling]], [[Spinoza Conatus]] |
90	
91	### Notes the table can't hold
92	
93	**`hub` is earned and can be lost.** The Weave proposes promotion at ≥5 inbound typed links and demotion back to `concept` if the degree falls below. Never self-assign it.
94	
95	**`person` entries are embodiable citizens** (v1.14). The *body* is the fully-formed human — source material an agent can wear in a [[Dialectic]] or [[Excellent Adventure]] — while the *frontmatter* is a newborn palace resident with its own `forward_vector` and usually an `agency_profile`. So a `person`'s `stage` tracks **palace citizenship** (born `seed`, growing through dispatch and enchantment), not the human's completeness — the same move `specialist` and `maker` make with `status`. The research corpus lives in a bundle `dossier`. Method: [[Making a Palace Citizen]].
96	
97	**`specialist` and `maker` skip `pillars` and `stage`.** They are tool-citizens, not idea-citizens; auto-tagging every Specialist `[tools]` would dilute the pillar signal, and they use `status` (alive \| stub) rather than the seed→fruiting lifecycle. Add `pillars` only when one genuinely participates in another pillar. Why they are two types and not one: [[SCHEMA — Context]] §3.2.
98	
99	**`meta` should stay few and high-quality.** These entries maintain the organism; inflation here is how a type system starts describing itself instead of the work.
100	
101	**A ceremony is a page that carries `trigger:`** — the words Loudon says to begin it — whatever its type; most are `practice`, a few are `meta`. It carries its own `version`, which moves only when its spec changes, never on a run ([[SCHEMA — Reference]] §6). A ledger does not make a page a ceremony: any page may keep one (§8). One ceremony is two pages — [[Closing Well Ceremony]], the card the agent who hears the trigger reads, and [[Closing Well]], the practice the fresh moderator runs, which carries the field.
102	
103	*(`breakthrough` was retired in v1.17 — see [[SCHEMA — Context]] §1.)*
104

106	
107	## 2. Development Stages
108	
109	Every entry has a `stage` in its YAML frontmatter reflecting its lifecycle. Stages are proposed by the operator and confirmed by Loudon. The Weave is the primary ceremony for stage transitions.
110	
111	```
112	seed → sprout → growing → mature → fruiting → dormant → composting
113	```
114	
115	| Stage | Meaning | Typical word count |
116	|---|---|---|
117	| `seed` | The idea has a name and a minimal body. Origin noted. | 50–150 words |
118	| `sprout` | A genuine definition exists. 1–2 typed links. | 150–400 words |
119	| `growing` | The idea has cross-domain connections. 3+ typed links. | 400–800 words |

# SCHEMA — The Palace Type System

![[SCHEMA — hero.png]]

The authoritative TBox for the Palace: what can exist here, and how things can be related. This card is
the **what exists** — the first thing an agent reads when it grows up ([[ELDER]]). A child recognizes the
palace without it; an elder reads it before touching the palace's structure.

**Before you write, read [[SCHEMA — Reference]].** The frontmatter fields (§3), the Schema Change
Protocol (§5), the ceremony-file conventions (§6), the entry-bundle spec (§8), and the [[STIGMERGY]]
coordination wire (§9) live there. They are the rules you need at the moment you create an entry, write
frontmatter, make a bundle file, post to the board, or change the type system — and at no other moment,
which is why they sit apart from this card (v1.18). Section numbers did not change; a `SCHEMA §8` pin still means
§8, now in the Reference. Do not write frontmatter from memory of this card.

**Schema changes are permanent structural commitments.** They require a Schema Ceremony
([[SCHEMA — Reference]] §5), documented rationale, and a version increment. Adding entries and editing
content are routine. Changing the schema is not.

> The **why** — every `v1.x` record, what changed in each section and the rationale behind it — lives in
> [[SCHEMA — Context]], keyed by section. A Weave or a Schema Ceremony reads it there. An operating agent
> reads the current rules, not the archive.

---

## 1. Entry Types

Every entry declares exactly one `type`. **Frontmatter is the canon membership card** — carrying it is what makes a `.md` file an entry. A file *without* frontmatter is not an entry but a learning material, draft, or artifact: invisible to the type system and the ceremonies. The boundary is permeable — a material graduates into canon when it earns an entry.

### The types

Read the table top to bottom and take the first row that fits; `concept` is the default when none do. The **test** column is the question to ask — it replaces the decision tree this section used to carry separately. The **adds** column is the type's extra required fields, on top of the standard set (`title`, `type`, `pillars`, `born`, `stage`, `links`).

| type | use it when — the test | adds | example |
|---|---|---|---|
| `meta` | it is about the palace itself: architecture, ceremonies, infrastructure, self-model | `version` (schema-level entries, ceremonies) · `trigger` (ceremonies) | [[SCHEMA]], [[SUBSTRATE]], [[CLAUDE]] |
| `specialist` | it wraps an external creative tool with operational anatomy — Charter, Tiers, Job Contract, accumulated Gotchas | `status` · `medium` · `tool` · `tool_version` | [[Shop/Kokoro]], [[Shop/ComfyUI]] |
| `maker` | it is a foreman for a roster of Specialists, holding house standards and dispatch logic | `status` | [[Shop/Maker]] |
| `source` | it is an external artifact the palace draws from — paper, book, tool, recording | `author` · `year` · `medium` | [[Meaning and the Link (2014)]] |
| `project` | it is being built, composed, or created; it has a temporal arc | `status` (active \| complete \| archived) | [[BLUELINE]], [[Loudon Live]] |
| `question` | it is an unresolved question being actively carried | — | *"When does the wiki warrant its own Project?"* |
| `spore` | it is an idea preserved for a later revival, dormant by choice (`stage` is always `dormant`) | `revival_conditions` | [[Shimmer Cloud]] |
| `hub` | it organizes a dense region of the graph — **not self-assigned**, earned at ≥5 inbound typed links via the Weave | — | [[FOUR PILLARS]], [[Kuramoto Coupling]] |
| `practice` | it is a recurring method, workflow, ritual, or embodied way of working — something you *do*, not an idea you hold | `version` · `trigger` (ceremonies) | [[Closing Well]], [[Deposit Ceremony]] |
| `person` | a thinker or collaborator whose ideas are in live dialogue with the palace — not every cited name | `domains` | [[Spinoza]], [[Brian Eno]] |
| `concept` | **the default.** An idea, principle, or framework the palace reasons with | — | [[Kuramoto Coupling]], [[Spinoza Conatus]] |

### Notes the table can't hold

**`hub` is earned and can be lost.** The Weave proposes promotion at ≥5 inbound typed links and demotion back to `concept` if the degree falls below. Never self-assign it.

**`person` entries are embodiable citizens** (v1.14). The *body* is the fully-formed human — source material an agent can wear in a [[Dialectic]] or [[Excellent Adventure]] — while the *frontmatter* is a newborn palace resident with its own `forward_vector` and usually an `agency_profile`. So a `person`'s `stage` tracks **palace citizenship** (born `seed`, growing through dispatch and enchantment), not the human's completeness — the same move `specialist` and `maker` make with `status`. The research corpus lives in a bundle `dossier`. Method: [[Making a Palace Citizen]].

**`specialist` and `maker` skip `pillars` and `stage`.** They are tool-citizens, not idea-citizens; auto-tagging every Specialist `[tools]` would dilute the pillar signal, and they use `status` (alive \| stub) rather than the seed→fruiting lifecycle. Add `pillars` only when one genuinely participates in another pillar. Why they are two types and not one: [[SCHEMA — Context]] §3.2.

**`meta` should stay few and high-quality.** These entries maintain the organism; inflation here is how a type system starts describing itself instead of the work.

**A ceremony is a page that carries `trigger:`** — the words Loudon says to begin it — whatever its type; most are `practice`, a few are `meta`. It carries its own `version`, which moves only when its spec changes, never on a run ([[SCHEMA — Reference]] §6). A ledger does not make a page a ceremony: any page may keep one (§8). One ceremony is two pages — [[Closing Well Ceremony]], the card the agent who hears the trigger reads, and [[Closing Well]], the practice the fresh moderator runs, which carries the field.

*(`breakthrough` was retired in v1.17 — see [[SCHEMA — Context]] §1.)*

---

## 2. Development Stages

Every entry has a `stage` in its YAML frontmatter reflecting its lifecycle. Stages are proposed by the operator and confirmed by Loudon. The Weave is the primary ceremony for stage transitions.

```
seed → sprout → growing → mature → fruiting → dormant → composting
```

| Stage | Meaning | Typical word count |
|---|---|---|
| `seed` | The idea has a name and a minimal body. Origin noted. | 50–150 words |
| `sprout` | A genuine definition exists. 1–2 typed links. | 150–400 words |
| `growing` | The idea has cross-domain connections. 3+ typed links. | 400–800 words |
| `mature` | The entry is stable, well-connected, unlikely to change fundamentally. | 800+ words or conceptually complete |
| `fruiting` | Actively generating new entries or connections. | Any stage can fruit. |
| `dormant` | Not currently active but preserved deliberately. | — |
| `composting` | Being broken down; nutrients being redistributed to other entries. | — |

**Composting protocol:** Before deleting any entry, mark it `stage: composting` for one Weave cycle. During the next Weave, confirm deletion or revive. This prevents accidental loss.

**`foundational`** is a reserved stage for palace meta-entries (CLAUDE, JEWEL, ELDER, SCHEMA, README, Substrate Skill) that are structural and do not follow the seed-to-mature lifecycle. These entries persist as long as the palace exists.
